page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities due to the single-core constraint. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the average category, with the AMD EPYC processor delivering stable single-threaded execution. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, register in the poor and weak categories respectively, as there are no additional cores to scale parallel workloads. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 21.24 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 18.37 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom decile or quartile of tested hardware.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers dedicated CPU resources at a low entry point, making it suitable for lightweight, non-parallelized tasks. Tradeoffs include low database operations performance and limited static web serving throughput of 1.73 GB/sec. It is best suited for basic utility workloads, single-threaded background workers, lightweight text processing, or small-scale development and testing environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand high memory bandwidth or multi-core scaling.
description: The Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance powered by a single dedicated core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4.0 GB of RAM, with no bundled local storage or GPU resources. Benchmark data indicates average single-core CPU performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1484.0 and average single-threaded compression speeds. However, due to its single-vCPU limitation, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are weak to poor, with static web serving throughput reaching 1.73 GB/sec and database operations scoring low. This instance represents a cost-efficient option for entry-level dedicated compute needs. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and small-scale development tasks that do not require parallel processing or high memory throughput.
